cards.text: Proverbs opens as the proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel (Prov 1:1). Here a father talks straight to his son. "My son, do not forget my teaching," he says, and let your heart keep my commandments.

cards.question: The father says his commandments will add something to his son's life if he keeps them. What do they add?

cards.text: Then he names two things his son should never let leave him: loving devotion and faithfulness. Bind them around your neck, he says, the way I wear this apron, and friend, I NEVER take it off.

cards.question: Besides binding loving devotion and faithfulness around his neck, where does the father tell his son to write them?

answers.text: On the tablet of his heart
On the doorposts of his house
On a scroll in the temple

cards.question: True or false: The father says holding on to loving devotion and faithfulness brings favor with God but not with people.

cards.text: Now the line folks hang on their walls in fancy fonts: "Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding". Friend, my own understanding once told me the oven was already hot, and I stood there TWENTY minutes watching cold dough do absolutely nothing.

cards.question: Instead of leaning on his own understanding, the father tells his son to ___ the LORD in all his ways.
True or false: The father says that when his son acknowledges the LORD in all his ways, the son will have to make his own paths straight.

cards.text: Next he says don't be wise in your own eyes. I was wise in my own eyes once and stamped FORTY cookies with my mustache hanging in the way, so that's forty cookies wearing forty MUSTACHES.

cards.question: Instead of being wise in his own eyes, what two things does the father tell his son to do?

answers.text: Fear the LORD and turn from evil

cards.question: True or false: The father says fearing the LORD and turning away from evil will bring healing to his son's body.

cards.text: Then he gets to money: honor the LORD with your wealth, he says, and your barns will be filled with plenty and your vats will overflow with new wine.

cards.question: Along with his wealth, the father tells his son to honor the LORD with the ___ of all his crops.

cards.text: "My son" again, and here's the part nobody hangs on their wall. Do not reject the discipline of the LORD, the father says, and do not loathe His rebuke.

cards.question: Why does the father tell his son not to reject the LORD's discipline?

answers.text: The LORD disciplines the one He loves
The LORD rewards those who suffer quietly
The LORD's patience will soon run out

cards.question: True or false: The father compares the LORD's discipline to a father disciplining a son he delights in.

cards.text: Now the picture changes: "Blessed is the man who finds wisdom". From here on, wisdom gets talked about like a person, a SHE, with a whole RÉSUMÉ coming.

cards.question: The father says wisdom is ___ than silver and fine gold and even rubies.

cards.text: Then he says nothing you desire compares with her. Friend, I'd put a fresh tray of chocolate chip cookies up against ANYTHING, so wisdom beating that is... okay, okay, I hear you.
Next, wisdom is pictured holding something in each hand. Riches and honor are in her left.

cards.question: Riches and honor are in wisdom's left hand. What does she hold in her right hand?
True or false: The father says all of wisdom's ways are pleasant and all her paths are peaceful.

cards.text: Then he calls her "a tree of life to those who embrace her". Those who lay hold of her are blessed.
And then the father zooms WAY out. Past the barns, past the treasure, all the way back to how the LORD made the world.

cards.question: After all that praise for wisdom, the father says the LORD founded the earth by ___.
True or false: The father says that by the LORD's knowledge the watery depths were sealed shut.

cards.text: It's the opposite, friend: "By His knowledge the watery depths were broken open, and the clouds dripped with dew." From the deepest waters to the morning dew, His knowledge has ALL of it handled, which is more than I can say for me and my timer.

findings.problem: The apron comparison sits inside the father's paraphrased words ('Bind them around your neck, he says, the way I wear this apron'). It reads as if the father in Proverbs is talking about Papa Dorin's apron, so the joke and the Bible setting run together.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: The verse is about binding something around the neck. An apron isn't the thing Papa Dorin wears around his neck. His neckerchief is. Because the image doesn't match the action of binding around the neck, the comparison doesn't click right away.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Fear the LORD and turn from evil', is the only one that mentions the LORD and the only one that sounds like Scripture. The wrong answers, 'Study hard and speak less' and 'Seek counsel and wait patiently', sound like general advice. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card cites Proverbs 3:13-18 but only tells verse 13 ('Blessed is the man who finds wisdom'), plus a general note that wisdom is called 'she.' The content of verses 14-18 is told on later cards (5, 6, 7, 9, 10). The citation is wider than what this card tells.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'smaller' and 'cheaper' are silly next to a passage praising wisdom as a treasure. A baker can rule them out without thinking, so the card tests nothing. Wrong answers need the same tone as the right one, such as other believable comparisons.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'It's the opposite, friend:' and requotes the verse 20 line that card 13 just tested. That re-explains card 13's answer, which is a recap, before it gets to the new detail about the dew. The new detail is the only part that moves the passage forward.
